title: The Energy Drink That Made a Man's Jaw Fall Off
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: The Energy Drink That Made a Man's Jaw Fall Off

lines.prompt: A rich 1920s American businessman in a sharp suit drinking from a small glass bottle that glows faintly green, art deco office

lines: In the 1920s, a wealthy American named Eben Byers drank a health drink every single day.

lines.prompt: Close-up of a 1920s glass bottle of tonic water glowing green on a silver tray, sparkles

lines: It was called Radithor. Distilled water, with radium dissolved in it.

lines.prompt: A 1920s advertisement-style scene, a smiling man flexing muscles next to a giant glowing bottle, sunburst background

lines: Radioactive drinks were sold as a source of energy and youth. Byers drank around fourteen hundred bottles.

lines.prompt: X-ray style view of a human skeleton glowing green in the bones, dark background

lines: But radium acts a lot like calcium. Your body puts it in your bones, and it stays there, giving off radiation.

lines.prompt: The same businessman now thin and frail sitting in a dim hospital room, his jaw wrapped in bandages, a doctor looking worried

lines: His bones began to break down. He lost most of his jaw. He died in 1932.

lines.prompt: A 1932 newspaper being read by a shocked man in a hat on a city street

lines: His death shocked America, and helped bring in stronger laws about what medicines could contain.
